sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Missouri, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Wednesday, October 21Passed

A request sent by mail, fax or email, or brought in by a relative or guardian, must reach your local election authority by 5 p.m. on the second Wednesday before the election: Wednesday, October 21, 2026, which is today as this is written. In person, you can apply and vote at the election office until 5 p.m. on Monday, November 2, 2026. (the law)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must reach your local election authority by the time the polls close on Election Day: 7 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A ballot that arrives later is not counted (military and overseas ballots have a later deadline). (the law)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Monday, November 2, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Missouri’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in Missouri or in another state? What Missouri says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

To vote absentee by mail you must give one of the reasons the law lists: you will be away from your county (or city election area) on Election Day; illness or disability, or caring at the same address for someone who is ill or disabled; religious belief or practice; working for the election office, or as a first responder, health care worker or law enforcement officer; being in jail while keeping the right to vote; or taking part in the state's address confidentiality program. From the second Tuesday before the election (Tuesday, October 20, 2026), anyone registered may vote absentee in person without giving a reason. (the law)

How to ask for a ballot

  • By mail. Send a signed written request to your local election authority (your county clerk or city or county election board, not the Secretary of State) by mail, fax or email. It must give your name, the address where you are registered, your reason, and where to mail the ballot. If you registered by mail and have not voted in person before, include a copy of your ID unless you already sent one. (official page)
  • In person. Apply and vote in person at your local election authority's office or the place it names. A guardian, or a close relative (such as a spouse, parent or child), may also apply in person for you. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it (or send it by a delivery company) in the ballot envelope to your local election authority, in time to arrive by 7 p.m. on Election Day. (the law)
  • In person. Hand it in yourself at your local election authority, or have a close relative (within the second degree, such as a spouse, parent or child) hand it in for you. Missouri law does not allow drop boxes for absentee ballots. (the law)

What the envelope needs

For most reasons, the statement on your ballot envelope must be signed in front of a notary public (or another official who can give oaths). No notary is needed if you are voting absentee because of illness or disability (or caring for someone who is), if you are in jail, if you are a military or overseas voter, or if you vote in person at the election office with photo ID. Voting absentee in person requires an acceptable photo ID; without one you can cast a provisional ballot. (the law)

Vote early in person instead

Tuesday, October 20, 2026 to Monday, November 2, 2026.

From the second Tuesday before the election, Tuesday, October 20, through Monday, November 2, 2026 (5 p.m. at the election office), any registered voter may vote absentee in person, with no reason, at a place the local election authority names. Bring a photo ID. (official page)

Students

At school in Missouri, away from home

The Secretary of State's How to Vote page does not speak to students separately. Under state law, being away from the county or city where you are registered on Election Day is one of the reasons that lets you vote absentee by mail, so a student registered at home who is at school in another part of Missouri can give that reason; with that reason, the envelope must be notarized. (the law)

At school in another state, with Missouri as home

The Secretary of State's How to Vote page does not speak to students separately. A Missouri voter who is out of state on Election Day can use the reason "away from my election area on Election Day" to ask for an absentee ballot mailed to them; with that reason, the envelope must be notarized. (the law)

Military and overseas

Military voters on active duty (and family living with them) and Missourians living abroad can use the Federal Post Card Application to register and ask for a ballot in one step; one request covers the primary and the general election, and no notary is needed. For November 3, 2026, the federal guide says the request must be received by Friday, October 30. A mailed ballot must be postmarked by Election Day and still arrive by the third day after (the law says before noon on Friday, November 6, 2026). Email or fax return is allowed only from a hostile fire area (places the Secretary of State lists), and must arrive by 7 p.m. on Election Day. (federal guide)

Missouri in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The deadline to ask for a ballot by mail, fax or email is 5 p.m. today, Wednesday, October 21, 2026. After that, the way left is to vote absentee in person at your local election office through 5 p.m. Monday, November 2, or to vote at your polling place on Election Day.
  • Section 115.277 was changed by a 2026 law that took effect August 28, 2026; the reasons above are from the version in force now.
  • No statewide ballot tracker was found on an official page; ask your local election authority about your ballot's status.
  • The Federal Voting Assistance Program's state guide was read through the content feed its own page loads.

How this was checked

  • The Secretary of State's site turned away a request with a check for human visitors; its How to Vote page was read through an ordinary fetch tool that was answered normally.
Where this comes from: 7 pages of Missouri’s election office, its laws and the federal guide

  2. How to Vote, Missouri Secretary of State (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  3. Missouri Revised Statutes 115.279, Application for absentee ballot, Missouri Revisor of Statutes (the law; read October 21, 2026)
  4. Missouri Revised Statutes 115.293 and 115.407, Absentee ballots counted when received by poll closing; polls open 6 a.m. to 7 p.m., Missouri Revisor of Statutes (the law; read October 21, 2026)
  5. Missouri Revised Statutes 115.291, Procedure for absentee ballots; return; no drop boxes, Missouri Revisor of Statutes (the law; read October 21, 2026)
  6. Missouri Revised Statutes 115.279 (6), 115.291 (2) and 115.920, Military and overseas ballots, Missouri Revisor of Statutes (the law; read October 21, 2026)
  7. Voting Assistance Guide, chapter 2: Missouri, Federal Voting Assistance Program (federal guide; read October 21, 2026)

Checked October 21, 2026. Rules and dates can change: Missouri’s election office, and your county or local election office, have the final word.
